title: Tallahassee World XC Course: Sand, Mud and Water
excerpt: The 2026 World Cross Country Championships course in Tallahassee featured sand, mud and water sections. What it shows about training for uneven terrain.
body:
The 2026 World Athletics Cross Country Championships were held on January 10 at Apalachee Regional Park in Tallahassee, Florida, on a course redesigned for the event. World Athletics described rolling hills and forest with sand, water and mud sections and obstacles inspired by local wildlife. LetsRun reporters who ran the course beforehand said they had never seen a mud pit like it on a US cross country course.

Courses like this reward strength, balance and the ability to change rhythm, not just raw speed. Runners who only train on smooth roads tend to lose time wherever the footing changes.

Add one off-road or trail run a week to your training. Running on grass, dirt and uneven ground builds the ankle stability and footwork that carry over to cross country, trail races and even a rough road shoulder.

Sources: LetsRun.com course guide; World Athletics
keyTakeaway: Regular running on uneven ground builds the balance and footwork that rough courses demand.
